item.title: Man caught on video kicking sea lion pleads guilty, faces prison time
item.description: Tyler Muehl, 18, pleaded guilty in federal court after a viral video captured him attacking the sea lion at La Jolla Cove.

item.title: Extreme weather slams the Midwest and in Indiana floodwaters are rising again
item.description: The Midwest is bracing for more extreme weather after flooding inundated entire streets in some areas. CBS News' Ian Lee reports.

item.title: Some schools are scaling back on how much they rely on screens in the classroom
item.description: As students across the country head back to the classroom, some schools, educators and parents are rethinking how much they utilize technology and screen time. Nicole Valdes has more.

item.title: Flock CEO apologizes, outlines changes amid claims its data was misused by police in some cases
item.description: Flock CEO Garrett Langley apologized in an interview with CBS News amid claims the surveillance company's license plate readers have been misused by some police officers. Langley also addressed new safety measures that were recently announced. Anna Schecter reports.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy's journal entries read in court after emotional moments in murder trial
item.description: Lindsay Clancy, the Massachusetts woman in court for the alleged murder of her three children, heard parts of her journal being read out as part of the proceedings. This comes after an emotional week that included autopsy images of her children. Abby Patkin, a Boston.com reporter, joins CBS News with more details.

item.title: New details from NTSB explain why a Ryanair passenger was partially sucked out of window
item.description: The National Transportation Safety Board has released new details about what may have caused a window to shatter on a Ryanair flight, partially sucking a passenger out of the window. Kris Van Cleave reports.

item.title: Outgoing Apple CEO Tim Cook discusses new U.S. manufacturing, job impact and more
item.description: Jo Ling Kent spoke exclusively with outgoing Apple CEO Tim Cook about a new manufacturing plant in Houston, what it means for jobs, and what he wants his legacy to be as he prepares to step down as CEO.

item.title: Sailor's dad expresses concern over conditions, length of deployment on USS Lincoln
item.description: There are growing concerns about conditions aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln from families of sailors and members of Congress. After more than nine months at sea, sailors' families say it lacks basic supplies and is affecting mental health. Charlie D'Agata reports.

item.title: Hawaii under a hurricane warning as Tropical Storm Lala takes aim
item.description: Tropical Storm Lala could bring heavy rain, high winds and dangerous surf and rip currents to the Hawaiian Islands as a hurricane this weekend, forecasters say.

item.title: UAE accuses Iran of Hormuz attacks as Vance says cheap gas is "goal number one"
item.description: The UAE accuses Iran of attacking two vessels in the Strait of Hormuz as Vance says cheap oil and gas is "goal number one" from the war.

item.title: Luigi Mangione's potential plea deal in federal trial sparks double jeopardy concern
item.description: Luigi Mangione, the man accused of killing UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson in New York City, is expected in federal court as sources say he may plea guilty. Legal analyst Joe Tamburino joins with more details about the questions concerning the future of his New York state trial.

item.title: Mangione may reach a plea deal in his federal case. Here's what it means for his state charges
item.description: Luigi Mangione, the man accused of killing UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson, is expected in court on Friday for a special hearing that could include a potential plea deal on federal stalking charges. Tom Hanson has more.

item.title: Hegseth reacts to scary concerns about USS Abraham Lincoln shortages and bad conditions
item.description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is reacting to concerns about food shortages and other apparent stark conditions aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln, which has been deployed for more than 250 days. CBS News' Zak Hudak reports.

item.title: Rivers swell in Indiana, breaking records set over a century ago and causing major flooding
item.description: There's been more than 11 inches of rain in parts of Indiana since Tuesday, leading to major flooding and evacuations. Ian Lee has the latest.

item.title: Hawaii County mayor braces for Lala's potential hurricane fury
item.description: Hawaii County Mayor Kimo Alameda joined CBS News with more emergency preparedness details as Tropical Storm Lala approaches and could soon become a hurricane.

item.title: Eye Opener: Flooding devastates parts of the Midwest
item.description: Heavy rain causes major flooding and damage in parts of the Midwest. Plus, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth responds to reports of poor conditions on the USS Abraham Lincoln. All that and all that matters in today's Eye Opener.

item.title: Tropical Storm Lala threatens Hawaii with harsh flooding and potential hurricane status
item.description: Tropical Storm Lala is headed toward Hawaii and may be a hurricane by the time it makes landfall. CBS News' Jarred Hill has more.

item.title: Evidence of bird strike on plane where man was nearly sucked out window, NTSB says
item.description: A bird strike may have been the cause of an incident in which a passenger was nearly sucked out of a broken window aboard a Ryanair flight in Europe last month, the NTSB found.

item.title: Costa Rica sends top drug trafficker, fellow cartel member to U.S.
item.description: Gilbert Bell Fernandez thanked the U.S. for taking him out of Costa Rica, claiming he had been mistreated in prison.

item.title: Tehran says Strait of Hormuz "under Iran's control" after Trump threat
item.description: Tehran has asserted that the Strait of Hormuz is "under Iran's control and management" after President Trump said the U.S. might "keep it."

item.title: American missionary kidnapped in Niger in October is freed, his group says
item.description: An American missionary who was kidnapped in Niger in October has been released, his organization says, adding that Kevin Rideout "is in good health in the care of U.S. officials."

item.title: Luigi Mangione in talks about possible guilty plea with court date today, sources say
item.description: Luigi Mangione, accused in the 2024 killing of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson, is in discussions about a possible plea deal on federal charges, sources familiar with the matter told CBS News.

item.title: Democratic senators demand answers about conditions aboard USS Abraham Lincoln
item.description: Senate Democrats are demanding answers about conditions aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln during the aircraft carrier's record-setting deployment.

item.title: Flock CEO responds to abuses of its surveillance technology
item.description: The CEO of Flock Safety apologized for alleged abuses of its service by law enforcement officers as the company rolled out new changes to how it operates.

item.title: Kennedy Center board votes to restore Trump's name on building
item.description: The Kennedy Center's board of trustees voted to add President Trump's name to the facade of the performing arts center, more than two months after a judge ordered its removal, according to a Democrat who sits on the center's board.

item.title: Jury selected for Tupac Shakur murder trial, opening statements expected Monday
item.description: A jury of six men and 10 women was selected to hear the case against an ex-gang leader accused of orchestrating Tupac Shakur's killing​ nearly 30 years ago.

item.title: Record-breaking heat takes mounting toll on the U.S. economy
item.description: Heat waves are dealing a financial blow to businesses and creating hazardous conditions for workers, according to climate experts.

item.title: Baby in surrogate dispute now in custody of parents, lawyer says
item.description: The baby at the center of a surrogacy dispute was born in Texas Wednesday and has hypoplastic left heart syndrome, a rare heart defect.

item.title: Trump administration's antisemitism lawsuit against Harvard dismissed
item.description: The lawsuit was one of many steps against Harvard that the Trump administration has taken since President Trump's return to office, in addition to attempting to cancel billions of dollars in federal funds.

item.title: Cities propose new tactics to crack down on so-called "teen takeovers"
item.description: Large gatherings of young people, often spurred by online invites, can lead to violence and injuries, even death.
